Dunmore Resale resells genuine towels it bought from the brand (D-4) with its own photographs: 17 U.S.C. 109(a) lets the owner of a lawfully made copy sell it, and nothing of the brand's photographs is copied
The photos are the seller's own and show a different towel; no work of the brand's is copied, and "Marrowby-style" in a title does not make a copyright claim
The listing was removed on 2 October 2026 by the seller; there is nothing left to take down
The photographs are the seller's own and copy nothing; the claim is counterfeit goods, which goes through Stallwick's trademark form, not a copyright notice

Unbranded towels with a copied photograph: no mark is on the goods, so the claim is a copyright notice, not a trademark complaint
Genuine goods from an authorised retailer: not counterfeit
Genuine goods the brand sold (D-4): a trademark complaint against them would be false
The goods carry Quillfeather's own label; "Marrowby-style" in the title is a name only, and Stallwick's trademark form says a listing that only names the brand is not a trademark complaint
Genuine Marrowby towels from a retailer whose photo licence ended; the goods are not counterfeit, the photograph is the issue
A title that says "like Marrowby" on the seller's own towels with its own label and photos: a name only, neither a copied photograph nor a counterfeit
